subject: research/infra-dcopf
professional: a power-systems optimisation researcher reviewing for IEEE Trans. Power Systems. First checks: is 'the DC OPF' the standard B-theta model and is its objective right against an independent solver; is the AC reference a validated optimum (PGLib/MATPOWER published values) under the same limit definitions; is the AC-feasibility check of the DC dispatch (power flow, MVA ratings, slack limits) computed correctly; are the counts in the headline the counts in the result files; and is the finding new against Stott et al. 2009, Baker 2021 and the successive-LP / loss-factor literature

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with code the author did not write. (1) Auditor's own B-theta DC OPF (own .m parser, own bus-balance/flow/angle rows, solved as a QP by HiGHS 1.16 via highspy; indep_dcopf.py) on six PGLib cases in both susceptance conventions: case14 API 4664.36 (MATPOWER B) / 4797.60 (PowerModels b=x/(r2+x2)), case118 API 234168.63 / 231291.91, case30 API 16185.06 / 16145.05, case30 TYP 7504.44 / 7472.81, case118 TYP 93132.68 / 93100.73, case14 TYP 2051.53: every value equals results_pglib.txt to the cent and the PowerModels-form values equal PGLib BASELINE.md (4.7976e+03 etc.), so the README's 'DC OPF is two models, 2.8 % apart on case14 API' finding holds. MATPOWER case118 DC OPF (pypower case data) 125947.87 = results.txt 125947.9. (2) Auditor's own Newton-Raphson AC power flow (own Ybus from the MATPOWER pi model, setpoints from PYPOWER runopf called directly; pf_check.py) on the auditor's DC dispatch: case14 API worst loading 109.0 %, 1 overload, slack 48.7 MW over Pmax; case30 API 119.9 %, 2, 0.0; case118 API 115.4 %, 9, 228.0: identical to results_pglib.txt. (3) PYPOWER runopf on MATPOWER case300 = 719725.08, the README's quoted published optimum. (4) run_pglib.py rerun in a scratch copy is byte-identical to results_pglib.txt (46 s). Not 4: the original IEEE-case section uses pandapower's AC OPF, whose 'AC optimum' I measured at 578.49 / 41872.30 / 129704.74 on case30/39/118 against MATPOWER's published runopf 576.89 / 41864.18 / 129660.69 (+0.28 / +0.02 / +0.034 %): pandapower limits branch current (one case30 line at exactly 100 % loading) rather than MVA, so the case30 headline 'DC dispatch 0.31 % cheaper than the AC optimum' is about 0.03 % against MATPOWER's optimum; and two counts in the PGLib section are wrong (claims).
evidence.completeness: Every script, result and figure the README names exists (scripted check over all experiments/*.py|txt|json|svg references: none missing). Test suite runs; run_pglib.py reproduces its committed table byte for byte; run.py reproduces all 37 committed rows of results.txt identically but now also writes 16 case300 rows not in the committed file (CASES in dcopf.py:17 includes case300). Live page https://marisstella.app/research/infra-dcopf/ returns 200 with the disclaimer text. 'Next steps' honestly lists what is not done (LMP decomposition, refresh rule, voltage/Q stage that is not a full AC OPF); refuted hypotheses (H2 on held-out cases, H4 convergence bound) are reported as refuted. I did not rerun the 20-30 minute vlin/heldout/perturb sweeps; their summary lines (31 of 34 by round 20, sign test P = 0.008 = binomtest(8,8) 0.0078) are consistent with results_converge.txt / results_heldout.txt.
evidence.verification: `cd research/infra-dcopf && OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 67 passed, 1 skipped (cyipopt missing) in 27.8 s. Tests pin results against outside numbers (PGLib published case118 AC objectives, published case14 API DC cost, a two-bus closed form, finite-difference vs analytic sensitivities, Clarabel vs PIPS on the same QP). Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 caught (penalty factor 1/(1-s) -> 1/(1+s); loss-factor sign in aclin.linearise; rating margin x1.05 in aclin.solve_linear; PowerModels convention keeping taps), 1 survived: the slack P-limit accounting in experiments/run_pglib.py:93 (Pmax x1.2) leaves every test green, and that number is the one the README misreports. Not 4: experiment-script logic that produces headline counts (run_pglib ac_check, the medians) is untested and nothing pins the committed result tables.
evidence.craft: Read src/infra_dcopf/dcopf.py (328 lines), aclin.py (184), pglib.py (95), experiments/run_pglib.py (first 100 lines), tests/test_dcopf.py, test_pglib.py. Small, documented functions with physical docstrings; correct QP Hessian scaling (2*c2 for qps_pips' 0.5 x'Hx); PYPOWER index constants used, not magic columns. Defects: dcopf.py:15 sets warnings.filterwarnings('ignore') at library import, silencing warnings for every importer; dcopf.py:52 and :61 catch every Exception and return None, so a coding error looks like 'no solution' (disclosed for solver failures, not for bugs); the penalty-scaling block is copied three times (dcopf.py:219, 305-308, 324-327); pm_convention, which the tests import, lives in an experiment script (run_pglib.py:47) rather than the package; README is a 445-line, 74 KB accretion log in date order, with the original IEEE-30/39/118 headline first and the stronger PGLib results below it.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: PGLib validation (AC within 0.004 % on 23 of 24, DC-PM within 0.003 %) = results_pglib.txt; DC cost gap medians 4.2 % TYP / 6.5 % API (recomputed medians 4.20, 6.47); overloads on all 11 API, worst 103-180 % (102.9-180.2); TYP overloads in 4 of 9; LMP median r 0.66 API / 0.96 TYP (0.655, 0.96); derating clears 1 of 11 (case57 at 0.85, +2.68 %); corrected_dc clean on 8 TYP / 1 API; case300 PYPOWER optimum 719725.08 = MATPOWER published; round budget 21 -> 31 of 34 = results_converge.txt. Wrong: README:27 'slack also runs past its P limit in 6 of 11 API cases (49 to 1,700 MW)': results_pglib.txt and the JSON show 8 of 11 (case14 48.7, case39 90.7, case73 128.8, case118 228.0, case162 180.8, case200 49.8, case240 1700.1, case300 795.0 MW). README:28 recall '(20 to 100 %)': case14 API recall is 0.00 (DC binds none of the 2 AC-binding lines), so 0 to 100 %. README:293 '59' tests and README:392 '52 tests, about 40 s' against 68 collected in 28 s. Method section (README:287-291) calls pandapower's runopp 'the AC OPF' without saying its limits are current-based or that its case30 optimum is 0.28 % above MATPOWER's. IPOPT DOI marked 'from memory'. Disclaimer present (modelled benchmark, AI assistance, safety note README:307).
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher wanting a reproducible DC-vs-AC OPF error study on standard benchmarks, or a starting point for AC-feasibility repair of a linear dispatch. Delivered: PGLib v23.07 cases vendored, AC reference validated against published optima, both DC conventions, per-case tables in JSON, pre-registered predictions in LOG.md, held-out SAD and 500-2,000-bus sets, refutations reported. I re-derived the core PGLib numbers from scratch in under an hour, which is what building on it requires. Nearest prior work: Stott, Jardim and Alsac 2009 (cited; DC flow error); Baker 2021, 'Solutions of DC OPF are never AC feasible' (ACM e-Energy, arXiv:1912.00319; not cited), which already establishes the 'DC dispatch AC-infeasible on every case' result in general; Castillo et al. 2016 SLP for IV-ACOPF and Misra/Molzahn adaptive linearisations (cited in the grid-linopf PROPOSAL, not this README); iterative loss-factor SCED as run by ISOs (Litvinov et al. 2004, 'Marginal loss modeling in LMP calculation', IEEE TPWRS 19(2); not cited). New and sound: the quantified MATPOWER-vs-PowerModels DC discrepancy on PGLib (useful, reproducible, though known to PowerModels users) and the honest held-out failure of the repair. Not publishable as a TPWRS paper on its own: one AC solver for most results, voltages from the AC optimum (oracle) for the headline repair counts, and the repair is a variant of known SLP.
evidence.domain: Against standard practice (MATPOWER manual DC/AC OPF formulations; PGLib-OPF benchmarking protocol; Wood and Wollenberg penalty factors): B-theta DC with 1/(x tap) and phase-shift injections matches MATPOWER makeBdc (my independent build agrees to the cent); AC check uses MVA ratings at both ends, angle limits and slack P limits; penalty factor 1/(1 - dPL/dPi) is the textbook form; AC optima validated against PGLib to 0.004 % and the larger cases' validation is tabled per case. Departures: the early IEEE-case section relies on pandapower's current-limited OPF and its own case conversions without reconciling to MATPOWER's published optima (0.28 % on case30); the power-flow check does not enforce generator Q limits (disclosed and counted separately as Qviol); generator voltages for the DC-dispatch check are taken from the AC optimum, which favours DC (disclosed); 'no solution' rows conflate infeasible and non-converged (disclosed). A TPWRS reviewer would accept the PGLib methodology and ask for the pandapower section to be reconciled or dropped.

verdict: A careful, reproducible benchmark study whose core numbers are right: an independent DC OPF (HiGHS) reproduces every PGLib DC objective in both susceptance conventions to the cent, an independent Newton power flow reproduces the AC overload, worst-loading and slack figures of the DC dispatch exactly, run_pglib.py reproduces its table byte for byte, and 4 of 5 seeded bugs are caught by a 68-test suite anchored to published values. It misses the bar on claims: the PGLib section misstates two counts (slack over limit on 8 of 11 API cases, not 6; recall range 0 to 100 %, not 20 to 100 %), test counts have drifted, and the original IEEE-case section treats pandapower's current-limited OPF as the AC optimum without reconciling it to MATPOWER's published optima (0.28 % off on case30, which is most of a headline number). As research it is a sound, incremental replication-and-repair study; the infeasibility finding is known (Baker 2021, uncited) and the repair is a variant of successive LP, so it is buildable-on but not a novel TPWRS result.
